Container.Name: NASlab-Agent
Container.Overview:
Read-only monitoring agent for the NASlab Android app. It measures your server every 30 seconds (temperature sensors, CPU load, GPU usage, RAM, network, disk spin-ups and which programs caused them, top processes, cache usage per share) and keeps a file index for searching all shares. History: 8 days at full resolution, 2 years of hourly values, stored in /config.
Beta: tested on Unraid 7 (amd64); arm64 untested.
It never changes anything on your server: every host path is mounted read-only, only /config is writable, root is dropped after start (PUID/PGID), and the container runs read-only with almost all capabilities removed. Optional and off by default: SMART values (NZBLAB_SMART), backup discovery for extra paths (NZBLAB_BACKUP_PATHS), redacted log excerpts (NZBLAB_LOGS), home-network device list (NZBLAB_LAN: every 30 minutes one empty UDP packet to each address of your /24 network to fill the ARP table, reverse DNS for new devices, push for new devices if ntfy is set). Service discovery (Sonarr, Radarr, Prowlarr, SABnzbd, Tautulli, Overseerr/Jellyseerr) reads API keys from appdata read-only and hands them to the app over the token-protected API; Plex tokens are never read; turn it off with DISCOVER_KEYS=0. The agent never updates itself.
After the first start, open the container log: the line "NZBLab-Agent Token: ..." appears once. Paste the token into the app (Settings, Server connections, NASlab-Agent). The token is also stored in appdata/nzblab-agent/token.txt. A read-only browser dashboard runs on port 8099. Do not expose this port to the internet; use a VPN (WireGuard, Tailscale) when away from home.
License: the agent is free and open source (GNU AGPL-3.0-only), source code on GitHub. The NASlab app is a separate, closed-source Android app (Google Play).
Deutsch: Misst Temperaturen, CPU, Grafikchip, RAM und Plattenzugriffe rund um die Uhr für die NASlab-App. Nur lesen, ändert nichts am NAS. Den Token zeigt das Container-Log beim ersten Start einmal, danach steht er in appdata/nzblab-agent/token.txt.
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: nzblab naslab monitoring temperature smart disk spin-up android app
Container.Changes: 1.18.0: push (ntfy) now only for critical things by default (disk failed, array stopped, CPU too hot); NZBLAB_NTFY_ALL=1 adds info messages; same alert at most once per 24 hours unless worse; log redaction also covers user names in PAM/sshd lines. Security hardening: the home-network device scan is now off by default (NZBLAB_LAN=1 turns it on); the 'Today' timeline shows no system log lines unless log excerpts are on, and then with IPs, MACs, e-mails, user names and paths removed; /config ownership is only changed in the agent's own or an empty folder (otherwise a warning); a correct token is never blocked by the failed-token brake. 1.17.0: sensor limits from hwmon, Synology disk names (sata1...), mover state from the system log (only with log excerpts on). 1.16.1: token hardening (min. 32 characters), crashes endpoint needs the token, parser limits. 1.16.0: service discovery (Sonarr, Radarr, Prowlarr, SABnzbd, Tautulli, Overseerr) for one-step setup in the app. 1.15.0: reboot history, per-disk temperatures, RAID/pool status, network latency, backup discovery, optional SMART and log excerpts.
Container.Requires: The NASlab Android app (Google Play). Unraid 6.12 or newer.

Config.Name: Web/API port
Config.Description: Port for the app and the browser dashboard

Config.Name: Data (/config)
Config.Description: Required, read/write. The agent stores its token and history here; without it you get a new token after every update. History (SQLite), file index, settings and token.txt. The only writable path.

Config.Name: Shares (file index)
Config.Description: Read-only. Search across all shares, storage analysis, duplicates, media inventory, appdata sizes. appdata, system, domains and isos are skipped by the index.

Config.Name: Cache pool
Config.Description: Read-only. What is waiting for the mover, per share. Remove this path if you have no pool named 'cache' (more pools: variable CACHE_ROOTS).

Config.Name: Host /sys
Config.Description: Read-only. Temperature sensors and GPU.

Config.Name: Host /proc
Config.Description: Read-only. CPU load, top programs, disk activity.

Config.Name: Unraid notifications
Config.Description: Read-only. Unraid notifications for the 'Today' timeline.

Config.Name: System log
Config.Description: Optional, empty by default. To enable, set /var/log (read-only): errors from the syslog for the 'Today' timeline.

Config.Name: Docker container names
Config.Description: Optional, empty by default. To enable, set /var/lib/docker/containers (read-only): container names in the 'top load' list. Needs PUID=0 (the files are readable by root only). The files contain container environment variables; the agent only keeps the names.

Config.Name: Time zone
Config.Description: e.g. Europe/Berlin, America/New_York

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User the agent runs as after start (99 = nobody). 0 = root: needed only for container names and appdata folders of other containers with strict permissions.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group (100 = users)

Config.Name: Token (optional)
Config.Description: Best leave empty: the agent creates a random token on first start (container log and appdata/nzblab-agent/token.txt). If you set your own: at least 32 random characters, no spaces (shorter values are refused).

Config.Name: Heat alert (C)
Config.Description: Push via ntfy when the CPU stays above this temperature (Celsius) for 5 minutes

Config.Name: ntfy URL (optional)
Config.Description: e.g. https://ntfy.sh/a-long-secret-topic for push alerts while away

Config.Name: ntfy: all messages (optional)
Config.Description: 0 = push (ntfy) only for critical things: disk failed or new disk errors, array stopped, CPU above the critical limit. 1 = also info messages (cheap disk prices, new devices on the home network, 'back to normal'). The app shows the rest. The same thing is sent at most once per 24 hours unless it gets worse.

Config.Name: SMART (optional)
Config.Description: 1 = read SMART values of the disks (model, serial, power-on hours, reallocated/pending sectors, CRC/media errors, wear, temperature). Read-only: smartctl --scan and smartctl -a -n standby only, never self-tests, never writes, sleeping disks stay asleep. Needs the disks as devices and SYS_RAWIO, e.g. Extra Parameters: --cap-add=SYS_RAWIO --device=/dev/sdb (NVMe also --cap-add=SYS_ADMIN). Leave PUID as is: a small root helper only runs smartctl. 0 = off.

Config.Name: Log excerpts (optional)
Config.Description: 1 = the app may show recent error and warning lines from the System log path (/var/log, read-only). IP/MAC/e-mail addresses, tokens, passwords, user names and share paths are removed before anything leaves the agent; it never sends logs anywhere by itself. 0 = off.

Config.Name: Home-network scan (optional)
Config.Description: 1 = device list of your home network in the app. Every 30 minutes the agent sends one empty UDP packet (port 9) to each address of your /24 network so the server fills its ARP table, then reads that table, looks up names of new devices (reverse DNS via your DNS server) and, if you set a push address, reports new devices (name, IP, MAC). Needs /proc (read-only) or host network. Your router or IDS may report this as a port scan. 0 = off, nothing is sent.

Config.Name: Network latency
Config.Description: 1 = every minute, measure the TCP connect time to the router and to 1.1.1.1:443 (no data is sent, no extra rights). Shows in the app whether the router or the internet is slow. 0 = off.

Config.Name: Find services and API keys
Config.Description: 1 = the app can connect Sonarr, Radarr, Prowlarr, SABnzbd, Tautulli and Overseerr/Jellyseerr in one step: the agent reads their API key, port and URL base from the settings files in appdata (Shares path, read-only; no docker.sock). Only with the agent token, at most 10 requests per minute, never logged. Plex tokens are never read; Jellyfin/Emby keys must be created in their web UI. 0 = only list which services exist, without keys.

Config.Name: Backup paths (optional)
Config.Description: Comma-separated container paths of backup repositories (restic, borg, kopia) or backup log files (rsync, scripts), e.g. /host/backup. Add each one as an extra read-only path first. Only file names and times are read, never the backup contents. Empty = only search the shares for backup folders.

Config.Name: Listen address
Config.Description: Address the agent listens on inside the container. Keep 0.0.0.0 with bridge networking; use the LAN address with host networking, or 127.0.0.1 behind a reverse proxy.

Config.Name: Price country (optional)
Config.Description: Disk prices: CH, DE, AT, US, GB, ... Usually set from the app. Empty = no price lookups.
